areas.area_name: A18 Evaporation (spent liquor concentration: multiple-effect falling-film evaporators with feed flash, product flash and liquor inventory storage)
areas.purpose: Remove the water that enters the liquor circuit so the circuit stays in water balance. Sources are bauxite moisture, residue and hydrate wash water, lime slurry water, direct-steam condensate and gland/flush water. Part of the spent liquor is concentrated from ~245 to ~300-320 g/L caustic (as Na2CO3) and blended back to make digestion liquor at C ~270-290 g/L. Clean steam condensate is recovered for boiler feed and hot process condensate for washing. A caustic liquor inventory is held so that an evaporator-train descale or a digestion outage does not force a refinery rate cut. Design duty: ~420 t/h water evaporated (~1.75 t per t Al2O3) in 2 parallel trains of ~210 t/h. CHANGED from the draft: LP steam is ~112 t/h (range 100-125) instead of ~100 t/h, and steam economy is ~3.6-4.0 (including feed flash and product flash) instead of 4.0-4.5. The reason is a stage-by-stage heat balance of the backward-feed train (see process description item 3a).
areas.process_description:
1) Spent-liquor routing (A11/A18 interface decision). All spent liquor from precipitation/classification (A12/A13, ~3,050 m3/h at ~56-62 degC) first passes the A11 pregnant-liquor/spent-liquor heat interchangers. These add ~95-110 MW and the liquor leaves at ~80-88 degC. It then collects in two evaporator feed tanks (18-TK-001/002). About 55% (~1,700 m3/h) goes to evaporation. The other ~1,350 m3/h bypasses evaporation and goes to the digestion liquor blend tanks (18-TK-021/022). The A19 oxalate-depleted liquor (~300-400 m3/h, 45-50 degC) also returns to the feed tanks. Fine hydrate in spent liquor seeds gibbsite scale, so the feed is drawn from well-clarified overflow and the tanks are only gently agitated.

2) Backward feed with feed flash. Each train's feed pump (18-PP-001..004) delivers ~850 m3/h to the separator of effect 6, the coldest effect (~0.17-0.22 bar(a), liquor ~60-65 degC). The feed enters through a tangential flash inlet and flashes ~20 K, releasing ~30 t/h of vapour per train to the surface condenser. A bleed from each effect's recirculation-pump discharge, under level control, moves the liquor forward to the next hotter effect (6->5->4->3->2->1).

3) Each effect is a vertical falling-film calandria (18-EV-1x1..1x6). The recirculation pump lifts liquor to the distributor on the top tube sheet. The liquor runs down the inside of 10-12 m tubes as a thin film, heated by vapour condensing on the shell side. The water vapour released travels down the tube with the film and separates in the effect's vapour separator (18-VS). It then passes a chevron/mesh demister and heats the shell of the next colder effect. Effect 1 is heated by LP steam at 4-5 barg, desuperheated to ~5-10 K superheat. Typical temperature cascade: steam ~152-158 degC; liquor in effect 1 ~135-140 degC; ~10-12 K effective driving force per effect; boiling-point rise of Bayer liquor ~5-10 K per effect; last-effect vapour ~50-55 degC.

3a) Heat-balance note (why economy is ~3.6-4.0 and not ~5). The liquor-to-evaporation mass ratio is ~5:1 (~1,100 t/h liquor per ~210 t/h water per train). In backward feed every effect must also heat the incoming liquor by ~12-15 K. That sensible heat takes ~15-20 t/h of vapour equivalent per effect. The product flash and feed flash recover only part of it. Higher economy would need a 7th effect, product flash extended to ~80 degC, or mechanical vapour recompression (MVR) on the cold effects, all to be confirmed with the vendor.

4) Product liquor leaves effect 1 at ~135-140 degC and C ~300-320 g/L. It flashes through 4 product flash tanks (18-FT, ~10-11 K per stage) down to ~95-100 degC. Each tank's flash vapour joins the shell side of the matching effect (effects 2-5).

5) The strong liquor goes to the blend tanks (18-TK-021/022). There it is mixed with bypass spent liquor, 50% caustic make-up (A19) and the A19 causticised/purified returns to give digestion liquor (C ~270-290 g/L, A/C 0.36-0.38). The blend is pumped to the A06 digestion liquor tank and the A04 mill liquor tank. Two large liquor inventory tanks (18-TK-051/052) hold strong liquor and absorb dilute spent liquor during a train descale (~24-48 h) or a digestion outage, so the caustic concentration to digestion can be held.

6) Last-effect vapour and feed-flash vapour condense in a shell-and-tube surface condenser (18-CD-101/201) cooled by cooling-tower water. Liquid-ring vacuum pumps (18-VP) remove non-condensables (air, CO2, light organics/VOCs).

7) Condensates. Effect-1 steam condensate is clean. Conductivity and sodium analysers check it before it returns to the power house (A20), and it dumps automatically to process condensate if contaminated. Vapour condensates from effects 2-6, the flash tanks and the condenser carry trace caustic (pH ~9-11) and volatile organics. They are flashed through a cascade of condensate pots and collected in 18-TK-012. This is the single plant process-condensate (hot wash-water) tank, and it also receives the A07 flash-heater condensate (~230 t/h). From there the condensate goes to residue washing (A08), hydrate/seed washing (A13/A14), lime slaking (A20) and cloth washing.

8) Chemistry and scaling. Evaporation is a physical concentration step, but it raises supersaturation.
(a) Dissolved silica forms desilication-product (sodalite) scale, mainly in the hottest effects: 6 Na2SiO3 + 6 NaAl(OH)4 + Na2X -> Na6[Al6Si6O24].Na2X + 12 NaOH + 6 H2O (X = CO3, SO4, 2Cl, 2OH).
(b) Gibbsite scale forms in the cooler effects when A/C is high or fine hydrate seed is present: Al(OH)4- -> Al(OH)3 + OH-.
(c) At very high C, sodium carbonate, sulfate and oxalate salt out.
Each effect is descaled in rotation: caustic boil-out with hot spent liquor for gibbsite, inhibited dilute sulfuric acid for DSP, and UHP water jetting.

9) High-temperature (boehmitic, ~240-260 degC) plants differ. They recover more heat regeneratively, often run lower caustic, and often have a larger water load where live steam is injected directly. Some still use older multi-stage-flash or forced-circulation evaporators. This low-temperature design uses indirect live-steam liquor heaters in digestion (A06), which keeps the evaporation duty moderate.

equipment.name: Evaporator feed (spent liquor) tanks
equipment.function: Buffer heated spent liquor from A11 ahead of evaporation and digestion; split the flow between evaporation and bypass; receive A19 oxalate-depleted liquor.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each can be taken out for cleaning at reduced throughput; 18-TK-052 provides back-up volume)
equipment.type_selected: Vertical flat-bottom cone-roof atmospheric storage tank, API 650 with Annex M (elevated temperature), with low-speed mixer
equipment.why_this_type: Gives large, low-cost surge volume (~2-3 h) that decouples precipitation from the evaporators. This is standard for Bayer liquor.
key_dimensions: ~4,000 m3 working each; ~20 m dia x ~14-15 m shell height (engineering estimate)
Roof slope ~1:16 cone; bund wall ~1.5-2 m high around both tanks (>=110% of the largest tank)
equipment.working_principle: This is a simple atmospheric surge tank. Heated spent liquor from the A11 interchangers enters near the top through an internal down-comer. Two bottom suction nozzles feed the evaporator feed pumps and the bypass pumps. A slow side-entry or top-entry mixer keeps fine hydrate in suspension so it does not build up on the floor, without the high shear that would create more fines. The level is used to balance the incoming flow against the evaporation rate. The liquor gives off steam and odour, so the tank vents to a common vent header.
details_to_model: Cylindrical carbon-steel shell with visible horizontal weld seams (~8 courses of 1.8-2 m), clad insulation (aluminium-zinc sheeting over ~50-75 mm mineral wool) on shell and roof
Cone roof with handrail ring, 2 roof manways (DN600), radar level nozzle, vent nozzle (DN300) to the vent header, emergency vent hatch
Spiral stair on the shell exterior with 2 intermediate landings; roof platform
2 shell manways DN900 at the base (diametrically opposite) for cleanout
Inlet nozzle DN600 near the top with internal down-comer; 2 outlet nozzles DN500 ~0.5 m above the floor with vortex breakers; A19 return nozzle DN300; drain/sump nozzle DN150
1 side-entry mixer (~30-45 kW) with motor and gearbox on a bracket near the base, OR a top-entry agitator bridge
Ring-wall concrete foundation, anchor chairs, earthing bosses, bund floor sloped to a sump pit with sump pump
Tank nameplate, contents label 'SPENT LIQUOR - CAUSTIC - HOT', safety shower within 10 s travel of the bund access
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic liquor (~14% NaOH equivalent, ~85 degC): severe chemical and thermal burns and permanent eye damage. Full PPE (face shield, goggles, PVC/rubber gloves, caustic suit) for sampling and opening.
Confined-space entry: isolate, drain, wash, ventilate and gas test; scale on the floor; positive isolation (spades) of all nozzles
Hydrogen: never use aluminium tools or scaffold inside caustic tanks (Al + NaOH releases H2)
Overflow/overfill: independent high-high level trip on the inlet; bund sized at 110%
instrumentation_and_control: Radar level (LT) + independent HH level switch
Temperature (TT)
Density meter on outlet (nuclear or Coriolis) for liquor control
Flow controllers on evaporator feed and bypass
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A516-70 / A283). Owner PWHT rule applies (design temperature >=65 degC in Bayer liquor): shop-PWHT nozzle/manway insert-plate assemblies (API 650 5.7.4) and PWHT attachment welds; full-shell PWHT is not normally done. Periodic wet fluorescent magnetic particle (WFMT) inspection of welds for caustic cracking. Verify against the NACE SP0403 chart (Area A boundary ~70-75 degC at ~14-17% NaOH, approximate).
common_problems: Hydrate settles on the floor and reduces volume
Corrosion under insulation at the bund-wall splash zone
operating_tips_and_key_points: Do not let the level run low: the feed pumps cavitate and lose suction
Check density and C, A/C every shift; spent A/C above 0.40 means poor precipitation and a high evaporator scaling risk
sources: Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry (Bayer flowsheet) - verify
API 650 Welded Tanks for Oil Storage, incl. Annex M
NACE SP0403-2015 Avoiding Caustic Stress Corrosion Cracking of Refinery Equipment and Piping (caustic soda service chart) - verify boundary values

equipment.name: Evaporator feed pumps
equipment.function: Pump spent liquor from the feed tanks to the effect-6 separator of each train under flow control.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal process pump (ISO 5199 heavy duty, OH1/OH2), VSD-driven
equipment.why_this_type: The liquor is clean and low in solids and the head is moderate, so a VSD gives energy-efficient flow control.
key_dimensions: ~850-950 m3/h at ~35-45 m head each; motor ~160-200 kW, 4-pole (engineering estimate)
Suction DN400-450, discharge DN300-350
equipment.working_principle: The closed impeller gives the liquor velocity, and the volute converts it to pressure. The VSD sets the speed to hold the evaporator feed flow at its setpoint, which ties the evaporation rate to the plant water balance. The installed spare is on auto-start with its suction and discharge valves open, and a check valve stops reverse flow through it.
details_to_model: Baseplate on a grouted concrete plinth, with drip rim and drain to the bund
Back pull-out volute casing (duplex CD4MCuN or CS), yellow coupling guard, TEFC motor
Double cartridge mechanical seal with seal-support pot (API Plan 53A/53B) on a stand
Suction: eccentric reducer (flat on top), temporary cone strainer, DN450 isolation valve
Discharge: concentric reducer, swing check valve, isolation valve, pressure gauge with diaphragm seal
Magnetic flowmeter on each train's common discharge
Drain/flush connections with quick couplings for condensate flush
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic spray from seal failure: seal guard/splash shield; safety shower nearby
Rotating coupling: guarded; LOTO before maintenance
Hot surfaces ~85 degC: insulate or guard
instrumentation_and_control: VSD speed control from the evaporator feed FIC
Bearing temperature/vibration monitoring (online or by route)
Low suction pressure trip
equipment.materials: Casing duplex SS or CS; impeller CD4MCuN duplex; shaft sleeve duplex; seal faces SiC/SiC
common_problems: Seal leaks from caustic crystallising on the seal faces
operating_tips_and_key_points: Flush with condensate before shutdown so liquor does not crystallise in the casing
Run the standby pumps weekly
sources: ISO 5199 Technical specifications for centrifugal pumps, Class II

equipment.name: Falling-film evaporator effects (calandrias)
equipment.function: Heat-transfer bodies of the 6-effect evaporator trains. Steam or vapour condenses on the shell side and boils water out of the liquor flowing as a film inside vertical tubes.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 installed. One effect at a time can be isolated and bypassed for descaling at reduced train rate. During a full-train descale the other train runs at its maximum and the inventory tanks 18-TK-051/052 absorb the water imbalance.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical shell-and-tube falling-film evaporator with top liquor distribution box, backward feed
equipment.why_this_type: Falling film works at a low temperature difference with short residence time and high heat-transfer coefficients. There is no hydrostatic head, so there is no boiling-point elevation from liquid depth, which suits a 6-effect cascade. It is the dominant modern Bayer evaporation technology. Alternatives are older multi-stage-flash or forced-circulation units, and MVR falling film where cheap power favours electrification.
key_dimensions: Heat-transfer area ~1,300-2,500 m2 per effect (engineering estimate; check: ~20 MW / (U ~1.2 kW/m2K x ~10-14 K) = ~1,400-1,700 m2)
Tubes ~50 mm OD x 2.6-3 mm wall, 10-12 m long, ~800-1,500 tubes per effect, triangular pitch ~64 mm
Calandria shell ID ~2.3-3.2 m; overall body height ~18-22 m, including the top distribution chamber (~2 m) and the bottom vapour/liquor chamber with sump (~3-4 m)
Shell expansion bellows (single or double convolution) ~1/3 of the way down from the top tube sheet

operating_parameters.parameter: Wetting rate (film flow per tube perimeter)
operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; typical falling-film design rule

operating_parameters.parameter: Steam economy incl. feed and product flash
operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (stage-wise heat balance); CHANGED from 4.0-4.5

equipment.working_principle: The effect's recirculation pump sends liquor into the top chamber. A distribution plate (perforated plate or individual tube ferrules/swirl inserts) spreads an even film over the inside wall of every tube. On the shell side, steam (effect 1) or vapour from the previous effect condenses on the outside of the tubes and its latent heat passes through the wall into the film. The film boils at the effect's saturation temperature plus the liquor's boiling-point rise. Vapour and film travel down together, which thins the film and keeps the heat-transfer coefficient high. At the bottom the liquor collects in the sump and the vapour turns into the side duct to the separator. Shell-side condensate drains from the lower tube sheet to a condensate pot, and non-condensables are bled from vent nozzles in the coldest shell zone. A dry tube (film breakdown) scales very quickly, so recirculation always keeps a minimum wetting rate, independent of the forward flow.
details_to_model: Tall, slender vertical cylinder carried on a structural-steel support ring at ~1/3 height (lugs on the shell) in the evaporator structure
Top: domed or flat bolted cover with davit arm for removal; liquor inlet nozzle DN300-400 into the distribution box; inspection manway DN600; sight glass with wiper and lamp
Distribution plate with ferrules, visible when the cover is open (training cutaway: tube sheet with ~1,000 tube ends)

Shell: steam/vapour inlet nozzle DN800-1,400 (effect 1 smaller, DN500-700) with internal impingement plate; NCG vent nozzles DN50-80 at 2-3 levels; condensate outlet DN150-250 at the lower tube sheet; expansion bellows; pressure gauge and PSV on the effect-1 shell

Bottom: conical/torispherical lower chamber with a large side vapour outlet DN1,200-1,800 to the separator, liquor outlet DN400 to the recirculation pump suction, bottom manway DN600 for descaling access, drain DN100
Insulation on shell, top and bottom (mineral wool ~75-100 mm + aluminium cladding); all hot surfaces are clad
Platforms at top-cover level (with davit and hoist beam), at bellows/vent level and at bottom-manway level; caged ladders and a shared stair tower
Training cutaway: falling film inside the tubes, vapour core, shell-side condensate droplets, DSP scale layer in the hot effects
hazards_and_safety: Steam at 4-5 barg / ~155 degC and hot caustic liquor up to 140 degC: flashing and scalding if opened under pressure. Before breaking flanges, verify zero pressure, temperature < 50 degC and that the vessel is drained.
Vacuum effects: implosion risk if vacuum breakers fail; designed for full vacuum
Confined-space entry for descaling (tube sheet and bottom chamber): gas test for O2, LEL (hydrogen from acid cleaning, see 18-SK-001) and CO2
UHP water jetting of tubes (1,000-2,500 bar): trained crews, deadman controls, exclusion zone
Working at height on platforms ~20-25 m
instrumentation_and_control: Shell pressure/temperature per effect (PT/TT)
Liquor level in the bottom sump (DP or radar)
Recirculation flow (magflow) with low-flow alarm (dry-tube protection)
Forward-flow control valve to the next effect, on level control
Density meter on product (controls final C)
Steam flow (vortex/orifice) to effect 1 with pressure control
Conductivity on each condensate stream (tube-leak detection)
equipment.materials: Shell and liquor-side heads: carbon steel SA-516-70 with full PWHT (caustic SCC per NACE SP0403 and owner rule). Tubes: seamless carbon steel (SA-179/SA-214); some vendors use stainless steel in the cold effects. Tube sheets: CS. Gaskets: compressed graphite (caustic-resistant).
common_problems: DSP scale in effects 1-2 cuts U by 30-50% over 2-6 weeks
Gibbsite scale in the cold effects when spent A/C is high or fines carry over
Uneven distribution causing dry tubes and rapid local scale
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch the overall delta-T and steam-rate trend: rising steam pressure at constant rate means scale
Never cut recirculation below the minimum wetting flow
Descale in a planned rotation, with the caustic boil-out before the acid clean
Keeping spent A/C low and the feed free of fines is the best scaling prevention
sources: Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia (evaporation in the Bayer process) - verify
Smith P. (2009) The processing of high silica bauxites - review of existing and potential processes, Hydrometallurgy 98:162-176 (DSP chemistry)
TEMA Standards; ASME BPVC Section VIII Div.1 (shell-and-tube pressure design)
Dimensions, U-values and steam economy: engineering estimate (vendor confirmation required)

equipment.name: Vapour-liquid separators (one per effect)
equipment.function: Separate entrained liquor droplets from the water vapour leaving the bottom of each calandria before the vapour goes to the next effect's shell, protecting condensate purity. The effect-6 separators also take the flashing feed through a tangential inlet.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical separator with tangential/side vapour inlet, chevron (vane) or wire-mesh demister, and wash sprays
equipment.why_this_type: Caustic carry-over contaminates condensate, which then cannot go to the boilers or be used as wash water. Two-stage separation (gravity/centrifugal, then demister) is standard.
key_dimensions: ~4-6 m dia x 8-12 m tall; the cold effects are largest because vapour density is low under vacuum (engineering estimate)
Vapour inlet DN1,200-1,800 at mid-height; vapour outlet DN1,200-2,000 on top; effect 6: extra tangential feed-flash inlet DN350-400 with wear plate
equipment.working_principle: The vapour-liquor mixture enters through a large side nozzle and slows down in the large cross-section. Droplets fall out by gravity and centrifugal action and drain back to the recirculation suction. The vapour rises through the demister pad, where fine mist strikes the vanes or wires, coalesces and drains. Intermittent condensate sprays wash salt build-up off the demister. In effect 6 the feed liquor flashes on entry: the vapour joins the stream to the condenser and the liquor drops to the sump.
details_to_model: Large-bore vapour duct (DN1,200-1,800) from calandria bottom to separator, with expansion joint
Separator body with elliptical top head; top vapour outlet with a large-radius elbow to the next effect
Demister pad support ring and wash spray header (visible in cutaway)
Liquor return leg DN300-400 from the separator bottom to the recirculation pump suction, with level bridle
Manways DN600 at demister level and near the bottom, each with a platform
Insulation and cladding; sight glass at liquor level
hazards_and_safety: Same as the effects: vacuum/pressure and hot caustic
Demister replacement is a confined-space entry with work at height inside the vessel
instrumentation_and_control: DP across the demister (fouling indicator)
Level in the separator boot (LT)
Condensate conductivity downstream (carry-over indication)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel, PWHT; demister SS 316L or duplex; effect-6 feed-inlet wear plate in duplex
operating_tips_and_key_points: A conductivity rise in the next effect's condensate often means demister damage or flooding
Run the demister sprays at each shift change
sources: GPSA Engineering Data Book / vendor demister design practice (Souders-Brown sizing)

equipment.name: Effect recirculation pumps (with forward-transfer bleed)
equipment.function: Keep the tube film wetted by circulating liquor from each effect's sump to its top distributor. A bleed from the discharge, on level control, transfers liquor to the next hotter effect.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 installed (warehouse spare rotating assemblies; effect bypass allows change-out)
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal process pump, large capacity, low head (OH1/OH2)
equipment.why_this_type: High flow and low head. The liquor is at its boiling point, so NPSHr must be low; the pump sits well below the sump, giving ~6-10 m static suction head.
key_dimensions: ~800-1,500 m3/h at ~20-30 m head; ~90-200 kW motor, 6-pole (~990 rpm) for low NPSHr (engineering estimate)
Suction DN450-600, discharge DN350-450

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate from the wetting-rate rule (~1,000 tubes x 0.14 m perimeter x 2 kg/m.s = ~780 m3/h minimum)

equipment.working_principle: The liquor in each sump is at its boiling point, so the pump relies on static head (sump elevation above the pump) to avoid flashing at the impeller eye. The pump lifts liquor ~20 m to the top of the calandria. A control valve on a side branch passes forward flow to the next effect, set by sump level. The recirculation rate stays essentially constant to protect the wetting rate.
details_to_model: Pumps at grade under the structure, in a row along the train, each below its effect
Long vertical suction leg from the sump with large-radius bends, isolation valve and expansion joint
Discharge riser up the structure to the calandria top, with check valve, isolation valve, magflow meter and the forward-transfer control-valve branch
Seal pot / seal-water panel beside each pump; drip trays; coupling guards
Pump maintenance monorail or mobile-crane access lane
hazards_and_safety: Liquor up to 140 degC flashes to steam if released: never open a casing under pressure
Seal failure sprays hot caustic: splash guards and safety showers along the pump row
instrumentation_and_control: Recirculation flow FT with low-flow alarm and steam trip
Motor current, bearing vibration
Discharge pressure
equipment.materials: Casing CS/ductile iron or duplex; impeller CD4MCuN or high-chrome iron; double mechanical seal (Plan 53/54) with condensate barrier
common_problems: Cavitation when the sump level drops or the pressure dips
Scale on the impeller and casing
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep sump levels steady; a level swing upsets both wetting and NPSH
sources: Hydraulic Institute ANSI/HI 9.6.1 NPSH margin guideline

equipment.name: Product liquor flash tanks
equipment.function: Flash-cool the hot product liquor from effect 1 (~138 degC) in 4 stages to ~95-100 degC. The flash vapour goes to the shells of effects 2-5 to raise steam economy.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical flash vessel with tangential inlet, internal impingement baffle and demister
equipment.why_this_type: Recovers the product liquor's sensible heat without extra heat-transfer surface (~45-50 t/h of flash vapour per train) and delivers near-atmospheric strong liquor for storage.
key_dimensions: ~3-4 m dia x ~7-10 m tall each (engineering estimate)
Liquor inlet DN350; vapour outlet DN600-900; liquor outlet DN350
equipment.working_principle: Liquor that enters a vessel below its saturation pressure partly boils (flashes) until it reaches the boiling point at that pressure. The vapour leaves through a top demister to the shell of the effect at about the same pressure. The cooler liquor flows on, driven by the pressure difference and under level control, to the next flash tank.
details_to_model: Row of 4 progressively larger vessels stepped down in elevation beside the hot end of the train
Inlet nozzle with level-control valve upstream; vapour line to the effect shell, sloped without pockets
Guided-wave radar level and gauge glass; PSV and vacuum breaker on each vessel
Manway, top platform, insulation
hazards_and_safety: Hot flashing caustic liquor: a line break can create a scalding steam/liquor cloud
Erosion at inlet nozzles from flashing two-phase flow: inspect wall thickness
instrumentation_and_control: Level control to the next stage
Pressure indication
equipment.materials: Carbon steel with PWHT; wear-resistant inlet impingement plate (duplex or hard-faced)
operating_tips_and_key_points: A product temperature well above design after the last flash means a flash-vapour line is blocked or a valve is closed
sources: Engineering estimate; standard flash-train practice (see also A07 flash cooling)

equipment.name: Final (surface) condensers
equipment.function: Condense the effect-6 vapour and the feed-flash vapour under vacuum using cooling-tower water. This sets the vacuum and the total temperature span of the train.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal shell-and-tube surface condenser (vapour on the shell side, cooling water in 2-pass tubes), TEMA AES/BEM type
equipment.why_this_type: Keeps caustic-bearing condensate out of the cooling-water circuit. The alternative, a direct-contact barometric condenser with barometric leg and hot well, is cheaper and common in older plants, but it contaminates the cooling water with caustic and organics.
key_dimensions: ~2,500-4,000 m2 per unit; shell ~3.5-4.0 m dia x ~10-12 m long (engineering estimate)
Vapour inlet DN1,800-2,200 on top; CW nozzles DN700-900; condensate outlet DN200 to hot-well/condensate pot

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (~40-45 t/h vapour x ~2,370 kJ/kg)
engineering estimate for a tropical site (wet bulb ~27-28 degC)

equipment.working_principle: Low-pressure vapour enters the shell over a tube bundle and condenses on the cold tubes. Condensation shrinks the volume about 10,000-fold, which creates and holds the vacuum. Non-condensable gases collect in a baffled air-cooling zone and are drawn off by the vacuum pumps. Condensate drains to a hot-well and is pumped to the process condensate tank. Warmer cooling water or fouled tubes raise the condenser pressure, which reduces evaporation capacity.
details_to_model: Large horizontal cylinder on two saddles (one fixed, one sliding) at high level (~+18-22 m) so condensate drains by gravity
Bolted channel heads at each end with CW inlet/outlet nozzles, removable covers (tube-cleaning access) and lifting lugs
Large top vapour inlet with expansion joint from the effect-6 separator
Air-offtake nozzle to the vacuum pumps; condensate drain with loop seal to hot-well/condensate pot
Rupture disc / vacuum breaker; thermometers on CW lines; platforms at both channel ends
hazards_and_safety: Vacuum: designed against implosion; vacuum breaker fitted
A tube leak lets caustic into cooling water: pH/conductivity monitoring of CW return
Channel cover removal needs a lifting plan
instrumentation_and_control: Absolute pressure PT (controls effect-6 conditions)
CW inlet/outlet temperatures
Hot-well condensate level
equipment.materials: Shell CS; tubes SS 316L (or duplex 2205 if CW chloride is high; titanium only on the CW side, never in hot caustic); tube sheets CS clad or duplex
common_problems: Air leaks into the vacuum system
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check the vacuum against the CW temperature: a rising approach means fouling or air in-leakage
sources: HEI Standards for Steam Surface Condensers (reference)

equipment.name: Vacuum pumps (non-condensable gas removal)
equipment.function: Remove air and non-condensable gases from the final condensers and the effect-shell vent manifolds to hold the vacuum.
equipment.type_selected: Liquid-ring vacuum pump package with separator and seal-liquid cooler
equipment.why_this_type: Robust with saturated, wet gas and condensable slugs. The alternative is multi-stage steam ejectors (no moving parts, but they use steam).
key_dimensions: ~1,500-3,000 m3/h suction volume at ~0.12 bar(a); ~55-110 kW motor (engineering estimate)
Skid ~4 m x 2 m with separator tank ~1 m dia
equipment.working_principle: An eccentric impeller turns in a casing partly filled with seal liquid, which forms a rotating ring. As the impeller turns, the spaces between the vanes expand (suction) and contract (compression). Gas is drawn in through the port plate, compressed and discharged with some seal liquid to a separator. The liquid is cooled and recirculated, and the gas goes to the vent/odour-control system.
details_to_model: Skid with pump, motor, direct coupling, gas-liquid separator vessel, plate cooler and seal-liquid pipework
Suction line with isolation valve, check valve and vacuum gauge; discharge to the vent header
hazards_and_safety: Odorous, VOC-bearing vent gas: route to treatment
Rotating-equipment guards; noise ~85 dB(A)
instrumentation_and_control: Suction pressure
Seal-liquid temperature and flow
Motor current
equipment.materials: Ductile iron/SS casing; SS impeller
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the seal liquid cool; capacity falls quickly as it warms
sources: Vendor practice for liquid-ring vacuum pumps (generic)

equipment.name: Condensate pots, condensate cascade, clean and process condensate tanks and pumps
equipment.function: Collect shell-side condensate from each effect and flash it down in cascade to recover heat. Keep clean effect-1 steam condensate (to the boilers) separate from process condensate (to washing). 18-TK-012 is the single plant process-condensate tank and also receives A07 flash condensate. Pump both streams onward.
equipment.qty_operating: 12 pots, 2 tanks, 1 clean + 2 process condensate pumps
equipment.type_selected: Vertical condensate pots with level control; vented atmospheric condensate tanks; horizontal centrifugal pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Simple, standard practice. Segregation protects the boilers from caustic contamination. One owner for process condensate (A18) removes the A07/A18 duplication.
key_dimensions: Pots ~1.0-1.5 m dia x 2.5-3.5 m
18-TK-011 clean condensate ~150 m3 (~6 m dia x 6 m); 18-TK-012 process condensate ~1,200 m3 (~12 m dia x 11 m, ~1.5-2 h at ~650 m3/h) (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; set by boiler water chemistry

equipment.working_principle: Condensate drains from each effect shell into a pot that seals the vapour space while passing liquid on level control. Each pot drains to the next colder pot, where part of the condensate flashes to steam that rejoins the vapour system. Effect-1 steam condensate is kept separate and checked online by conductivity and sodium analysers. If caustic is detected (tube leak), actuated three-way dump valves divert it automatically to process condensate.
details_to_model: Row of small vertical pots under the effects, each with gauge glass, level transmitter and control valve
Two analyser cabinets with sample coolers near the clean condensate line
Actuated three-way dump valve with yellow position indicator
Tanks with vent stacks, ladders and insulation; pump sets at grade with guards
hazards_and_safety: Hot condensate and flash steam: burns
Caustic in boiler feed causes caustic gouging/embrittlement in boilers: the dump is a key interlock
instrumentation_and_control: Conductivity (plus Na analyser on the clean line)
Level controls
Temperature
equipment.materials: Carbon steel; analysers SS
common_problems: Analyser drift causing false dumps or missed contamination
operating_tips_and_key_points: Calibrate the conductivity analysers weekly; never bypass the dump interlock
sources: ASME CRTD-34 'Consensus on operating practices for the control of feedwater and boiler water chemistry in modern industrial boilers'

equipment.name: Strong liquor / digestion liquor blend tanks and transfer pumps
equipment.function: Receive strong evaporated liquor, bypass spent liquor and caustic make-up, blend them to digestion-liquor strength, and pump the blend to digestion (A06) and mill liquor (A04).
equipment.type_selected: API 650 (Annex M) atmospheric insulated tanks with top-entry agitator; horizontal centrifugal pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Provides surge between evaporation and digestion (~1.5-2 h) and is the blending point for controlling digestion caustic.
key_dimensions: ~3,000-3,500 m3 working each; ~18 m dia x ~14 m (engineering estimate)
Pumps ~1,000 m3/h x 50-60 m head, ~250 kW each
equipment.working_principle: The agitator mixes strong liquor at ~95-100 degC with bypass spent liquor at ~85 degC. Caustic make-up is added at the inlet to reach the target C, measured by an online density/conductivity correlation and checked by lab titration. The transfer pumps send liquor on flow control to the digestion liquor tank and the mill liquor tank.
details_to_model: Two insulated tanks in a common bund; agitator bridge on the roof with gearbox and motor
Labelled caustic make-up injection quill on the inlet; sample point with cooler and safety shower
Pump row with discharge header, flowmeters and isolation valves
hazards_and_safety: ~95 degC strong caustic (~17% NaOH equivalent): severe burns
Caustic make-up addition point: local high concentration and heat of dilution
instrumentation_and_control: Level, temperature, density/conductivity analyser
Caustic make-up flow-ratio control
equipment.materials: Carbon steel, PWHT per owner rule (above the NACE SP0403 Area A boundary at this temperature and concentration): shop-PWHT nozzle and insert assemblies, attachment welds PWHT, WFMT weld inspection
common_problems: Salt crystallisation (carbonate/oxalate) on cooler walls and roof
Caustic SCC at attachments that were not PWHT'd
operating_tips_and_key_points: Add caustic gradually and keep the agitator running

equipment.name: Liquor inventory (caustic inventory) storage tanks and transfer pumps
equipment.function: Hold the circuit's caustic liquor inventory. TK-051 normally holds strong liquor; TK-052 is kept partly empty to receive dilute spent liquor. During an evaporator-train descale (~24-48 h) or a digestion outage, strong liquor is drawn from inventory and surplus dilute liquor is stored, so digestion caustic and refinery rate can be held. Also used to adjust total soda inventory and to empty vessels for maintenance.
equipment.type_selected: Large vertical flat-bottom cone-roof atmospheric tanks, API 650 with Annex M, insulated, with side-entry mixers; horizontal centrifugal transfer pumps
equipment.why_this_type: The draft had only 1.5-3 h of surge, so a train descale (losing ~210 t/h of evaporation) would force a rate cut. ~24-48 h of inventory is common Bayer practice. Both tanks are piped so either can take either duty.
key_dimensions: ~12,000 m3 working each; ~32 m dia x ~17 m shell (engineering estimate). One train out for ~36 h leaves ~7,500 t of water unremoved, which needs ~8,000-10,000 m3 of dilute-liquor storage and a similar strong-liquor draw
Bund >=110% of one tank; ring-wall foundation; 3 x side-entry mixers ~45-55 kW per tank
equipment.working_principle: In normal operation TK-051 is kept ~70-80% full of strong liquor and TK-052 ~20-30% full. When a train is descaled, the blend tanks draw extra strong liquor from TK-051 to hold C at ~270-290 g/L, and an equal volume of surplus spent liquor goes from the spent liquor header into TK-052. After the descale both trains run at maximum, working TK-052 back through the evaporators until the inventory is restored. Side-entry mixers keep fine hydrate and salts in suspension.
details_to_model: Two very large insulated tanks (the largest in the area), with spiral stairs, roof handrail ring, radar level and HH switch, vents to the vent header, 4 roof manways
3 side-entry mixers per tank at the base, each with motor/gearbox bracket and a hinged maintenance platform
Shell manways DN900 x 3, inlet nozzles with internal down-comers, bottom outlets with vortex breakers, drain sump
Pump set at grade with flowmeters and remotely operated isolation valves (descale line-up from the DCS)
Bund with sump pump, safety showers, signage 'HOT CAUSTIC LIQUOR'
hazards_and_safety: Large inventory of hot caustic: tank failure or overflow is a major spill. Bund at 110%, HH trip, regular integrity inspection.
Confined-space entry for cleanout (heavy hydrate/salt sludge, heat): positive isolation, ventilation, gas test
Hydrogen from aluminium contact: no aluminium tools or scaffold
instrumentation_and_control: Radar level + HH switch, temperature, density on outlet
Inventory calculation in the DCS (total Na2CO3-equivalent tonnes in the circuit)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel, API 650 Annex M. Owner PWHT rule: shop-PWHT all nozzle, manway and insert assemblies; PWHT attachment welds; in-situ PWHT of the shell-to-annular-plate region and lower courses where practical; periodic WFMT inspection of welds for caustic cracking - verify approach with the tank vendor
common_problems: Caustic cracking at highly stressed welds if PWHT is incomplete
operating_tips_and_key_points: Restore the inventory set-points promptly after every descale so the next outage can be covered

equipment.name: Effect-1 steam control and desuperheating stations
equipment.function: Control LP steam flow and pressure to effect 1 and remove superheat (near-saturated steam gives better heat transfer).
equipment.type_selected: Steam pressure/flow control valve with spray-water (condensate) desuperheater
equipment.why_this_type: Standard practice. Condensing steam close to saturation gives the best shell-side coefficient and avoids hot spots that promote scale.
key_dimensions: Steam line DN500-600; control valve DN300-400; desuperheater spool with ~6-8 m straight run (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A control valve throttles LP steam to the pressure needed for the required evaporation rate. Downstream, atomised condensate is sprayed into the steam and evaporates, cooling it close to saturation. A temperature controller downstream sets the spray rate.
details_to_model: Steam header take-off with isolation gate valve, strainer, control valve with actuator and positioner, manual bypass globe valve
Desuperheater probe/nozzle with spray-water line and control valve; temperature element ~10 diameters downstream
Steam traps and drip legs; insulation; PSV on the effect-1 shell
hazards_and_safety: Steam at 155-170 degC: burns; water hammer if drains are not cleared at start-up
instrumentation_and_control: PT, TT, FT (vortex/orifice)
Evaporation-rate control: steam flow setpoint from the density/water-balance controller
equipment.materials: Carbon steel A106B piping; Stellite valve trim
operating_tips_and_key_points: Warm up and drain the lines slowly; open steam gradually after vacuum is established in the train

equipment.name: Evaporator descaling system (caustic boil-out, acid cleaning, UHP water jetting)
equipment.function: Remove DSP, gibbsite and salt scale from the evaporator tubes, separators, flash tanks and piping on a planned rotation.
equipment.type_selected: Fixed acid storage/make-up tank with circulation pumps and hoses; mobile UHP jetting units
equipment.why_this_type: Bayer evaporator scale is unavoidable. Inhibited dilute H2SO4 dissolves DSP (sodalite/cancrinite), hot spent liquor or caustic dissolves gibbsite, and UHP jetting removes hard deposits.
key_dimensions: Acid make-up tank ~50-80 m3 (HDPE/FRP or rubber-lined CS); circulation pumps ~150-250 m3/h; neutralisation pit (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; confirm with the chemical-cleaning vendor

equipment.working_principle: The effect is isolated, drained of liquor and flushed with condensate. Hot spent liquor or caustic is circulated first to dissolve gibbsite, then flushed out. Inhibited dilute sulfuric acid is then circulated to dissolve the aluminosilicate scale, with dissolved iron (a measure of steel corrosion) and acid strength monitored. Spent acid is neutralised with spent caustic before it returns to the process or goes to the residue system. Remaining hard scale is jetted out at 1,000-2,500 bar.
details_to_model: Acid tank with bund, acid unloading point, eyewash/safety shower, pumps on a skid
Flexible hose connections (hammer unions), temporary spools, blinds/spades
Vent hose from the vessel high point to a safe location, with portable LEL monitor
Mobile UHP jetting trailer with lances, foot-pedal dump valve and hose-whip restraints
hazards_and_safety: Acid cleaning of carbon-steel evaporator tubes releases hydrogen (Fe + H2SO4 -> FeSO4 + H2), plus CO2 from carbonate scale. Ventilate the vessel, keep ignition sources out, monitor LEL continuously during and after the clean, and vent the circuit to a safe location. H2S is not expected unless sulfide scale is present. Contact with zinc, galvanised steel or aluminium makes the H2 release much faster. Hydrogen release increases when the inhibitor is depleted.
Sulfuric acid and caustic in the same area: violent heat on mixing. Strict segregation and flushing between steps.
UHP water injection injuries; noise
Confined space (gas test for O2, LEL, CO2 before entry)
instrumentation_and_control: Acid strength (conductivity/titration), temperature, dissolved iron
Portable and fixed LEL monitoring at the vent and the entry point
Interlocks preventing liquor valves from opening to the acid circuit
equipment.materials: Acid tank FRP or rubber-lined CS; pumps alloy 20 or lined
common_problems: Corrosion and extra hydrogen when the inhibitor is under-dosed
operating_tips_and_key_points: Always complete positive isolation, and flush with condensate between the caustic and acid steps
Track dissolved iron during the acid step: a rising trend means the inhibitor is depleted
sources: Industry practice for Bayer heater/evaporator descaling (consistent with A06 06-SK-001: inhibited H2SO4, hydrogen hazard)

areas.layout_notes: Two evaporator trains stand side by side in one open steel structure, ~75-90 m long x 30-35 m wide x 28-32 m high (engineering estimate). The 6 calandrias of each train are in a straight row at ~10-12 m centres, supported at ~+8-10 m, each with its separator beside it. The 4 product flash tanks per train are stepped down at the hot end. The surface condensers are at high level (~+18-22 m) at the cold end so condensate drains by gravity, with the vacuum pumps below at grade. Recirculation and transfer pumps are at grade beneath their effects, in two rows with a central maintenance aisle (truck access for pump change-out). Platform levels are grade, ~+10 m (bellows/lower vents) and ~+22 m (top covers, davits), with stair towers at each end and an optional lift. The feed tanks (18-TK-001/002), blend tanks (18-TK-021/022) and condensate tanks are in an adjacent bunded tank farm ~20-40 m from the structure. The two large inventory tanks (18-TK-051/052, ~32 m dia) are in a separate bund ~50-100 m away on the A06 side. The area lies between the A11 heat interchange / A12 precipitation tank farm (~100-200 m) and digestion (A06, ~100-250 m). LP steam comes from the power house (A20, ~150-300 m), and the cooling towers are ~100-200 m away. A 3-tier pipe rack (+6/+9/+12 m) runs along one long side carrying spent liquor, strong liquor, steam, condensate, CW and the vent header. Clear lay-down areas at each end allow tube jetting and crane access (~100-200 t mobile crane for cover and bellows work).
interfaces: A11 Heat interchange: all spent liquor (~3,050 m3/h) is heated from ~58 to ~80-88 degC before 18-TK-001/002 (routing decision)
A12/A13 Precipitation/Classification: spent liquor source (via A11)
A06 Digestion: digestion liquor (blend, C 270-290 g/L) ~2,100-2,200 m3/h to 06-TK-101
A04 Grinding: mill liquor ~600-720 m3/h to 04-TK-020
A07 Flash: flash-heater process condensate (~230 t/h) to the single process-condensate tank 18-TK-012 (A18 owns it)

A19 Liquor purification: 50% caustic make-up into 18-TK-021/022; strong liquor side-streams to oxalate crystallisation (~150-250 m3/h) and the liquor burner (~15-25 m3/h); oxalate-depleted liquor (~300-400 m3/h) back to 18-TK-001/002; LBF leach return
A20 Utilities: LP steam ~112 t/h at 4-5 barg; clean condensate return ~112 t/h; cooling water ~5,000 m3/h; instrument air; 6.6/0.415 kV power
A08 Residue washing / A13-A14 hydrate washing / A20 slaking: process condensate ~650 t/h as hot wash water
Vent/odour control: NCG from vacuum pumps (optionally to the A19 RTO)
Laboratory: C, A, S, density, TOC, oxalate, condensate conductivity

areas.area_name: A19 Liquor purification (causticisation, oxalate removal, organics removal by liquor burning, caustic make-up)
areas.purpose: Hold liquor impurities at steady, acceptable levels and maintain the caustic inventory. (1) Causticisation: convert sodium carbonate back to caustic with slaked lime, holding C/S ~0.86-0.90. The carbonate comes from bauxite carbonates, CO2 uptake and organic degradation. (2) Oxalate removal: crystallise and remove sodium oxalate before it co-precipitates with gibbsite, which causes fines, poor hydrate quality and high soda in the product. (3) Organics (TOC) removal: destroy humic and other organics that raise viscosity, cut precipitation yield, discolour hydrate and stabilise oxalate. This uses a side-stream liquor burning facility (LBF), which also destroys the oxalate cake. (4) Caustic make-up: receive (by pipeline from the port), store and dose 50% NaOH to replace soda losses (~75 kg NaOH/t Al2O3). CHANGED from the draft: causticisation duty is ~25 kg Na2CO3/t (was 35) on a ~600 m3/h side-stream (was 500), because the carbonate in dilute washer liquor was overstated.
areas.process_description:
1) Causticisation (side-stream on dilute liquor, improved two-stage scheme).
A side-stream (~600 m3/h, range 450-750) of residue washer 1 overflow (C ~110-130 g/L as Na2CO3) goes to the causticisation feed tank at ~85-95 degC. It may be blended with washer 2 overflow, giving C 90-130 g/L. Washing dilutes the liquor but does not change C/S (~0.86-0.88), so the carbonate is only ~14-20 g/L as Na2CO3. Dilute liquor is used because the carbonate-hydroxide equilibrium favours conversion at low caustic concentration.
Reactor 1 (19-TK-111) receives slaked lime slurry from the A20 ring main and runs close to the feed temperature (~75-90 degC, short residence ~15-30 min). There the lime reacts with aluminate and carbonate to form hydrocalumite: 4 Ca(OH)2 + 2 NaAl(OH)4 + Na2CO3 -> Ca4Al2(OH)12.CO3.xH2O + 4 NaOH.
The slurry is then heated by direct steam injection (19-SI-101, ~8-15 t/h LP steam) to ~100-103 degC in Reactors 2-3 (19-TK-112/113, ~1.5-2 h). There the hydrocalumite reacts with more carbonate to give calcium carbonate and release aluminate: Ca4Al2(OH)12.CO3 + 3 Na2CO3 -> 4 CaCO3 + 2 NaAl(OH)4 + 4 NaOH. The net reaction is Ca(OH)2 + Na2CO3 -> CaCO3 + 2 NaOH.
The competing reaction to avoid is 3 Ca(OH)2 + 2 NaAl(OH)4 -> Ca3Al2(OH)12 (tricalcium aluminate, TCA) + 2 NaOH. It wastes lime and alumina, and it forms if hydrocalumite is held too long or too hot in high-aluminate liquor.
Carbonate falls by ~9-12 g/L (product C/S ~0.93-0.95). Carbonate removed is ~6 t/h Na2CO3 (~25 kg/t Al2O3; range 15-40). Lime efficiency is ~50-65% for conventional single-stage causticisation and ~80-90% for the improved scheme (licensor data, verify). Design uses ~75%, giving ~4.2 t/h CaO.
The causticised slurry (~6.5-7.5 t/h solids, mostly CaCO3) returns to the residue washer train (A08, washer 3 feed). The CaCO3 leaves with the residue, and the regenerated caustic is recovered up the washer train.

2) Oxalate removal. Sodium oxalate forms when humic organics degrade (in the bauxite and in digestion). It builds up to its critical stability limit (~3-5 g/L in spent liquor, depending on C, temperature and organics), above which it co-precipitates on the hydrate as fine needles. At this plant:
(a) Controlled co-precipitation onto the fine/tertiary seed is washed off with hot condensate in A13 seed washing, giving an oxalate-rich seed-wash liquor (~150 m3/h, Na2C2O4 ~5-10 g/L).
(b) This liquor is mixed with a side-stream of strong evaporated liquor (~150-250 m3/h). The high caustic lowers oxalate solubility (salting-out). The mix (~300-400 m3/h, C ~190-220 g/L, ~85-95 degC) is cooled to ~45-50 degC in wide-gap plate coolers (~15-20 MW) and crystallised in seeded, agitated crystallisers (19-CR-201/202, ~4-8 h, oxalate seed ~20-50 g/L). The mix A/C is kept at or below ~0.40 to limit gibbsite co-precipitation.
(c) A thickener separates the crystals. Most of the underflow is recycled as seed, and a bleed is filtered on a horizontal vacuum belt filter. The overflow (Na2C2O4 lowered by ~1.5-2.5 g/L) returns to the evaporator feed.
(d) The oxalate cake (~0.6 t/h Na2C2O4, equal to the net oxalate generation, plus adhering liquor) goes to the liquor burner, where 2 Na2C2O4 + O2 -> 2 Na2CO3 + 2 CO2. Sodium oxalate also decomposes above ~290 degC to Na2CO3 + CO.
Alternatives used in industry: lime destruction (Na2C2O4 + Ca(OH)2 -> CaC2O4 + 2 NaOH, with calcium oxalate disposed with residue) and biological oxalate destruction (reported at Worsley, WA - verify).

3) Organics removal: liquor burning facility (LBF). A strong-liquor side-stream (~15-25 m3/h, TOC ~20-30 g/L C) is concentrated in a forced-circulation evaporator (19-EV-301) to ~50-60% total solids. A pug mill mixes it with recycled burnt product and the oxalate cake into agglomerates, which are burned in a rotary kiln (19-KL-301) at ~900-1,050 degC (engineering estimate). The sodium organic salts oxidise (R-COONa + O2 -> Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O). In the hot zone, sodium carbonate reacts with alumina from the dehydrated aluminate: Na2CO3 + Al2O3 -> 2 NaAlO2 + CO2. Carbonate soda is therefore returned as caustic-equivalent aluminate.
The burnt product is cooled, dissolved in lean liquor (19-TK-311) and returned to the circuit. Kiln off-gas passes dust collection (ESP or baghouse), then a regenerative thermal oxidiser (RTO) to destroy VOCs and odour (cf. the RTO at the Alcoa Wagerup liquor burning facility - verify), then the stack.
Alternatives: fluidised-bed liquor burners (cf. Alcoa Kwinana - verify) and wet oxidation (~250-280 degC, ~80-110 bar, O2), which is not selected because of high pressure, corrosion and cost. East Coast India bauxite is low in organics, so the LBF can be smaller or deferred. Darling Range bauxite is organic-rich, which makes the LBF essential.

4) Caustic make-up. 50% NaOH is imported through the port (A17, bulk storage at the port) and pumped through an ~8 km pipeline to the refinery storage tanks 19-TK-401/402. A road-tanker unloading bay is the back-up. Caustic is dosed on ratio control to the strong liquor blend tanks (A18). Design rate is ~18 t/h NaOH (100% basis) = ~36 t/h of 50% solution (~24 m3/h); range 55-110 kg NaOH/t Al2O3 depending on reactive silica. Soda losses are: DSP (~0.69 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2), soluble soda in residue, soda in product (~0.3-0.4% Na2O), and oxalate/LBF/spills.

Note for high-temperature plants: boehmitic plants run lower caustic and higher temperature and add lime in digestion (forming cancrinite/hydrogarnet, which lowers soda loss and improves boehmite extraction). Their lime use is often higher and their causticisation arrangement differs.

equipment.name: Causticisation feed tank and feed pumps
equipment.function: Buffer the dilute washer-overflow side-stream and feed it at a controlled rate to Reactor 1.

equipment.name: Causticisation Reactor 1 (hydrocalumite formation)
equipment.function: Contact slaked lime with the dilute aluminate liquor under controlled, moderate-temperature, short-residence conditions to form hydrocalumite, the intermediate that makes the improved process efficient.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated, baffled, cylindrical atmospheric reactor tank with top-entry agitator
equipment.why_this_type: Well-mixed, short-residence contact disperses the lime quickly, so hydrocalumite forms rather than TCA.

Agitator ~30-55 kW, hydrofoil/pitched-blade impeller ~2.5 m dia, 4 wall baffles
equipment.working_principle: Lime slurry and liquor enter together near the impeller. Calcium hydroxide dissolves and reacts with aluminate and carbonate ions, precipitating hydrocalumite (Ca4Al2(OH)12.CO3.xH2O). This is a layered double hydroxide in which carbonate sits between positively charged calcium-aluminium hydroxide layers. Residence time and temperature are limited so the hydrocalumite does not convert to stable tricalcium aluminate. The slurry overflows to Reactor 2.
details_to_model: Tank with bridge-mounted agitator drive (motor + right-angle gearbox) on the roof; 4 vertical baffles

Insulation and cladding

Agitator: LOTO before entry; confined space
instrumentation_and_control: Temperature, level, agitator power
Lime:feed ratio controller
equipment.materials: CS with PWHT of welds per owner rule; agitator shaft/impeller CS with wear protection
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check lime efficiency daily (carbonate removed vs CaO added)

equipment.name: Oxalate crystalliser feed tank, pumps and feed coolers
equipment.function: Combine oxalate-rich seed-wash liquor with a strong-liquor side-stream and cool the mix to ~45-50 degC to create oxalate supersaturation.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated feed tank; wide-gap plate heat exchangers (cooling water)
equipment.why_this_type: Wide-gap plates tolerate fine solids and are easy to clean; cooling drives oxalate supersaturation.
key_dimensions: Tank ~300 m3 (~7.5 m dia x 7 m)

Total cooler duty ~15-20 MW (CHANGED from 8-14 MW): ~350 m3/h x ~1.3 t/m3 x ~3.2 kJ/kgK x ~40-45 K; LMTD ~28-30 K; U ~1.2-1.5 kW/m2K -> ~450-500 m2 total, i.e. 2 x ~250-300 m2 operating + 1 spare; each frame ~3.5 m tall x ~1.2 m wide x ~4-5 m long (engineering estimate)
Cooling water ~1,500-1,800 m3/h
equipment.working_principle: Sodium oxalate solubility falls as temperature falls and as caustic concentration rises (common-ion/salting-out effect). Mixing the low-caustic, high-oxalate wash liquor with strong liquor and then cooling it makes the mix supersaturated in oxalate. Keeping the mix A/C low limits gibbsite nucleation.
details_to_model: Plate packs between fixed and movable frame plates, with tie bolts, carrying/guide bars and 4 corner nozzles; spray shield over each pack
Tank with agitator; pumps with guards; CW connections with isolation valves
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic leaks at the plate gaskets: spray shield over each plate pack
instrumentation_and_control: Outlet temperature control (CW flow)
DP across each cooler (fouling)
equipment.materials: Plates SS 316L (suitable for this caustic at <~95 degC inlet, with CW chloride controlled). Titanium is NOT used because it is attacked by hot caustic. If CW chloride is high, use a closed tempered-water loop. EPDM gaskets.
common_problems: Oxalate and hydrate scale on the plates
operating_tips_and_key_points: When the DP doubles, switch to the spare cooler and caustic-wash the fouled one

equipment.name: Oxalate crystallisers

equipment.type_selected: Agitated, baffled crystalliser tanks (flat or shallow-cone bottom) with draft-tube or hydrofoil agitator
equipment.why_this_type: Seeded, well-mixed growth avoids fine nucleation, and the long residence completes desupersaturation.
key_dimensions: ~1,000-1,200 m3 each; ~11 m dia x 12 m (engineering estimate)
Agitators ~55-90 kW each
equipment.working_principle: Supersaturated liquor contacts a large surface of existing needle-shaped sodium oxalate crystals. Oxalate deposits on these seeds instead of forming new fines. Recycling thickened seed keeps the surface area high, and the liquor desupersaturates towards solubility as it passes through the two tanks.
details_to_model: Two large tanks with roof agitators, overflow launders between them, platforms
Seed recycle inlet; sample points; drain valves
hazards_and_safety: Caustic liquor (~45 degC, still corrosive)
Confined space with scaled internals
instrumentation_and_control: Temperature, level, solids density, oxalate (lab: IC or titration)

sources: Power, Loh & Vernon (2012) 'Organic compounds in the processing of lateritic bauxites to alumina Part 2: Effects of organics in the Bayer process', Hydrometallurgy 127-128:125-149

equipment.name: Oxalate thickener

Drive torque ~100-200 kNm class
equipment.working_principle: Feed enters a central feedwell, where it slows down and spreads out. Crystals settle to the floor, and slowly turning rakes move them to the central cone for underflow pumping. Clear liquor rises to a peripheral overflow launder.

2 underflow pumps (1 standby) with recycle and bleed lines

Rake bogging: torque alarm
instrumentation_and_control: Rake torque, bed level, underflow density
equipment.materials: CS
common_problems: Rake overload from oxalate scale build-up
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch rake torque trends

equipment.function: Dewater the oxalate bleed and deliver the cake to the liquor burner (or to lime destruction).
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal vacuum belt filter with cake wash (alternatives: pressure filter or pusher centrifuge)
equipment.why_this_type: Allows displacement washing of entrained caustic; simple to maintain.
key_dimensions: ~8-12 m2 filtration area; belt ~1.5-2 m wide x ~8-10 m long (engineering estimate)
Cake bin ~50 m3 with screw feeder

Filtrate receiver vessel, liquid-ring vacuum pump, filtrate pump
Screw conveyor to the cake bin; bin vent

equipment.name: LBF feed concentrator (forced-circulation evaporator)
equipment.function: Concentrate the strong-liquor side-stream to ~50-60% total solids before liquor burning, to cut kiln fuel.
equipment.type_selected: Single- or double-effect forced-circulation evaporator with external shell-and-tube heater and axial recirculation pump
equipment.why_this_type: High concentration and near-saturated salts mean heavy scaling. Forced circulation suppresses boiling in the tubes; falling film cannot handle these solids levels.
key_dimensions: Heater ~300-500 m2; separator ~3 m dia x 8 m; axial circulation pump ~2,000-3,000 m3/h, ~150-250 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A large axial pump drives the liquor at high velocity (2-3 m/s) through the heater tubes, under enough static head that it does not boil inside them. The liquor flashes in the separator instead, which keeps salt deposits out of the tubes.
details_to_model: Vertical separator, external heater (inclined or vertical), large elbow loop with the axial pump at the bottom, steam inlet, condensate pot, vapour line to the condenser
hazards_and_safety: Very concentrated hot caustic (~25-35% NaOH equivalent): severe burns
Salt blockages
instrumentation_and_control: Product density, level, steam flow
equipment.materials: Nickel alloy (e.g., alloy 200/201) or duplex in hot, concentrated zones; this service is in NACE SP0403 Area B/C, so PWHT CS is not adequate (engineering estimate - verify)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep density in range; overconcentration plugs lines

equipment.name: Liquor burner rotary kiln with feed pug mill and burner
equipment.function: Oxidise sodium organic salts and oxalate to sodium carbonate and convert the carbonate to sodium aluminate, destroying TOC and recovering soda.
equipment.type_selected: Direct-fired counter-current rotary kiln with twin-shaft pug-mill feed and natural-gas burner
equipment.why_this_type: Handles sticky sodium-salt agglomerates. Recycling burnt product dilutes the liquor so the bed does not melt. Alternatives: fluidised-bed liquor burner; wet oxidation.
key_dimensions: Kiln ~3.0-3.6 m shell dia x ~45-60 m long, slope ~2-3%, 2-3 tyres, girth-gear drive ~200-350 kW (engineering estimate)
Pug mill ~1.2 m x 6 m, twin shaft
Burner ~10-20 MW firing
equipment.working_principle: Concentrated liquor, oxalate cake and hot recycled product are mixed into damp granules and fed into the upper (cold) end of the inclined kiln, which turns slowly (~1-3 rpm). As the bed tumbles towards the burner end it dries, then the organics burn (releasing heat), and finally sodium carbonate reacts with alumina to form sodium aluminate. Hot gases flow counter-current to the bed and leave at the feed end.
details_to_model: Long refractory-lined steel shell on 2-3 tyre/roller stations, with thrust roller, girth gear and pinion, main drive motor + gearbox, and auxiliary (barring) drive
Feed-end housing with seal and feed chute from the pug mill; discharge (firing) hood with burner pipe, flame scanner and peep holes
IR shell-scanner gantry; kiln shell cooling fans
Platforms at each tyre station; roller lubrication systems
hazards_and_safety: Hot surfaces and flame; burner management system per NFPA 85/86 (purge, flame-failure trips)
Caustic dust; CO in confined zones; rotating machinery
Refractory relining: confined space and heat stress
instrumentation_and_control: Kiln inlet/outlet temperatures, O2/CO analyser, shell scanner, drive current, BMS
equipment.materials: Shell CS; alkali-resistant alumina brick/castable refractory
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the recycle ratio up to prevent melting and rings

Alcoa Kwinana and Wagerup liquor burning references (public environmental reports) - verify
NFPA 86 Standard for Ovens and Furnaces

equipment.name: LBF product cooler, leach (dissolution) tank and pumps
equipment.function: Cool the burnt product, dissolve its soluble sodium aluminate/carbonate in lean liquor, and return the solution to the circuit.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary drum cooler (or fluid-bed cooler); agitated leach tank; slurry pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Robust handling of hot granular product.
key_dimensions: Cooler ~2.5 m dia x 20 m (engineering estimate)
Leach tank ~150 m3

hazards_and_safety: Hot solids; caustic dust; exothermic dissolution
instrumentation_and_control: Temperature, leach density
equipment.materials: CS
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the leach tank agitated; lumps cause blockages

equipment.name: LBF off-gas cleaning: dust collector, regenerative thermal oxidiser, ID fan and stack
equipment.function: Remove sodium-salt dust and destroy VOCs/odour in the kiln off-gas before discharge.
equipment.type_selected: ESP or pulse-jet baghouse; 2- or 3-can regenerative thermal oxidiser (ceramic media beds); centrifugal ID fan; steel stack
equipment.why_this_type: VOC and odour emissions from Bayer liquor burning have been a documented community issue. An RTO destroys >95-98% of VOC with low fuel use.

operating_parameters.basis: US EPA RTO fact sheet range; engineering estimate

In the RTO, gas flows up through a hot ceramic bed into the burner chamber, where the VOCs oxidise, then down through a second bed that absorbs the heat. Valves reverse the flow every 1-3 minutes, so ~95% of the heat is recovered.

Hot surfaces; ESP high voltage (interlocked access)

LEL analyser
RTO temperatures, valve position switches

common_problems: Salt plugging of the RTO media
operating_tips_and_key_points: Bake out the RTO media periodically to clear salt plugging
sources: Alcoa Wagerup refinery liquor burning facility RTO (public reports c.2006-2007) - verify

equipment.name: Caustic soda (50% NaOH) pipeline receipt, back-up tanker unloading, storage and dosing
equipment.function: Receive 50% caustic by the ~8 km pipeline from the port tank farm (A17), with a road-tanker bay as back-up. Store ~20 days of supply and dose it to the liquor blend tanks and minor users (resin regeneration, scrubbers).
equipment.qty_operating: 1 pipeline receipt station; 1 back-up road-tanker bay; 2 tanks; 2 dosing pumps
equipment.type_selected: API 650 vertical cone-roof CS tanks, insulated, with low-temperature heating; horizontal centrifugal pumps (sealless mag-drive or double mechanical seal)
equipment.why_this_type: Standard caustic storage practice. Carbon steel without PWHT is suitable for 50% NaOH only below ~45-50 degC (NACE SP0403 Area A). Gentle heating prevents crystallisation (freezing point ~12 degC). Pipeline receipt follows the A17 decision and removes ~1,000 tanker movements a year.
key_dimensions: Tanks 2 x ~6,000 m3 (~22 m dia x 16 m); ~20 days at 24 m3/h (CORRECTED from '~14 days'); bulk import tanks are at the port (A17) (engineering estimate)
Bund >=110% of the largest tank, with alkali-resistant coating
Pipeline receipt: pig receiver, flow meter, filter, flush connection (condensate) for line displacement
Back-up bay: 1 road bay with canopy, ~25-30 t per tanker

operating_parameters.basis: Caustic handbooks (keep above ~15 degC); NACE SP0403 Area A limit for 50% NaOH ~45-50 degC

equipment.working_principle: Caustic arrives by pipeline from the port tanks in batches, through a filter and meter into the storage tanks. The pipeline is displaced with condensate and kept full or flushed during long stops so it does not freeze or crystallise. In a back-up delivery, the tanker is coupled with dry-break couplings and emptied by transfer pump into the tanks. Dosing pumps deliver caustic on flow-ratio control to the blend tanks, where it mixes into a large hot liquor stream, so the heat of dilution is small. Tank heating uses tempered water (~40 degC) or low-pressure steam coils with surface temperature limited, so there are no local hot spots above the no-PWHT limit.
details_to_model: Two large insulated tanks with tempered-water heating coil or bottom heating panel, spiral stair, roof handrail, radar level and HH switch, vent with breather and CO2 guard (prevents carbonate pick-up)
Pipeline receipt skid: pig receiver, meter, filter, isolation valves, flushing hose station
Back-up road bay with canopy, loading hoses, dry-break couplings, drip tray, wheel chocks, earthing clamp
Tempered-water safety showers and eyewash stations (alarmed) at the bay, the receipt skid and each pump set
Pump set with splash guards, discharge filters and magflows; DN100-150 transfer lines with flange spray guards
Signage: CORROSIVE class 8 (UN1824), PPE board
hazards_and_safety: 50% NaOH causes severe skin burns, and blindness within seconds. Flush for at least 15 min (eyes: up to 60 min) with urgent medical review.
Large heat of dilution: never add water to concentrated caustic
Spray from flange leaks: flange spray guards
Pipeline: overpressure/surge protection, leak detection, pig-receiver opening procedure
Heavy-vehicle movements at the back-up bay
Hydrogen from contact with aluminium
instrumentation_and_control: Level, temperature, flow; HH level trip closes the pipeline receipt valve
Pipeline leak detection (flow balance between port and refinery meters)
Shower-activation alarm to the CCR
equipment.materials: Carbon steel without PWHT, acceptable only because metal temperature is kept <=45-50 degC (NACE SP0403 Area A). EPDM/PTFE gaskets; SS 316 small-bore.
common_problems: Crystallisation in lines at low temperature
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never let the tank heating raise the metal temperature above ~45 degC
Wear full PPE when coupling and uncoupling; check the safety shower works before every transfer

Euro Chlor GEST guidance on caustic soda storage - verify
NACE SP0403-2015 caustic soda service chart (Area A/B/C)
ANSI/ISEA Z358.1 Emergency eyewash and shower equipment

areas.layout_notes: Causticisation (19-TK-101, 19-TK-111..113, pumps) is a compact bunded block (~45 m x 25 m) next to the residue washer train (A08), ~50-100 m from washers 1-3, so the feed and return lines stay short. Lime slurry comes from the A20 lime ring main (~100-300 m). The oxalate plant (~60 m x 40 m: feed tank, 3 plate coolers, 2 crystallisers, thickener, belt-filter house) sits between evaporation (A18, strong liquor) and seed washing/classification (A13), ~100-200 m from each. The liquor burning facility takes ~120 m x 40 m (concentrator, pug mill, ~60 m kiln, cooler, leach tank, ESP/RTO and a 40-60 m stack). It is on the downwind side of the refinery, at least 300 m from offices, control room and laboratory, near A18 for the strong-liquor feed, with road access for refractory work. The caustic tank farm (2 x 6,000 m3), the pipeline receipt skid and the back-up road bay sit at the refinery boundary where the port caustic pipeline enters, ~200-400 m from the liquor blend tanks (A18), with a dedicated caustic line on the main rack. Every area has bunds sloped to sumps, with sump pumps returning spills to the process, and safety showers within ~10 s travel (~15 m) of every caustic hazard point.

- Steam demand raised from 410 to 450-470 t/h (gibbsite dissolution endotherm in digestion; evaporator steam 112 t/h).
- HRSGs re-rated to ~95-100 t/h each and a third auxiliary boiler added, so steam capacity with the largest unit out (N-1) is ~500 t/h.
- Cooling water raised from 10,000 to ~16,000 m3/h (7-cell tower).
- Lime lowered from 40 to ~32 kg CaO/t.
The utilities are designed N+1 so that agitation and steam continue when a unit is lost. Settling of solids in precipitators and thickeners after a total power loss is one of the most costly refinery upsets.
areas.process_description:
1) Steam and power (cogeneration).
Two gas-turbine generators (~25-35 MW ISO class, ~80-100 kg/s exhaust at ~480-550 degC) exhaust into two single-pressure heat-recovery steam generators (HRSG) with duct burners. Each HRSG raises ~35-45 t/h unfired and ~90-100 t/h fired (duct-burner outlet <=850-900 degC) at ~63-65 bar(a) / 470-480 degC.
Check: 90 kg/s x ~1.15 kJ/kgK x (850 - ~140) K = ~73 MW; divided by ~2,800 kJ/kg = ~94 t/h. Reaching 150 t/h would need a fully fired water-wall HRSG, which is not selected.
Three gas-fired D-type package water-tube boilers (~150 t/h each, same steam conditions) make up the balance. Normally two fire at ~65-90% load and the third is on hot standby. Installed HP capacity is 2 x 100 + 3 x 150 = ~650 t/h. With the largest unit (one 150 t/h boiler) out, ~500 t/h remains, which covers the ~450-470 t/h demand.
HP steam passes through a back-pressure/extraction steam turbine generator (~40-50 MW), with MP extraction at 10-12 barg (~190 t/h to the digestion live-steam heaters) and LP exhaust at 4-5 barg (~260-280 t/h to evaporators, pre-desilication, causticisation, LBF concentrator, deaerators and tank heating). Pressure-reducing and desuperheating stations (PRDS) back up each level when the turbine is off.
Total generation (~100-110 MW) exceeds site demand (~65-72 MW), so ~35-40 MW is exported to the grid (gas cogeneration supplying Western Australian refineries, e.g. the Alinta Pinjarra cogeneration plant - verify). The site can island on grid failure.
Alternative, common at Indian refineries (Lanjigarh, Utkal, Damanjodi): coal-fired CFBC boilers with back-pressure turbines (higher CO2, ~0.8-1.0 t CO2/t alumina; needs a coal yard, ash handling and ESPs).

2) Boiler feedwater and condensate.
Clean condensate returns from the digestion live-steam heaters (~180-200 t/h), evaporator effect 1 (~112 t/h) and the LBF concentrator (~8-12 t/h), ~290-310 t/h in total. It is checked by conductivity and sodium analysers with automatic dump, then filtered and polished into the condensate tanks. Together with demineralised make-up (~120-180 t/h; direct-injection steam to pre-desilication, causticisation and hydrate wash heating is not returned), it is deaerated at ~1.5 barg / ~127 degC. The deaerators take ~45-50 t/h of LP steam.
Chemical treatment: oxygen scavenger, amine or ammonia for pH, and phosphate or all-volatile treatment as the boiler supplier specifies. Caustic ingress from a heater tube leak is the main boiler-chemistry risk (caustic gouging and caustic embrittlement).

3) Raw water.
Water is pumped from a dam or river (~10-30 km pipeline) into a lined raw-water storage pond (~7 days) and distributed to: cooling-tower make-up (~280-310 m3/h), the water treatment plant (clarifier, multimedia filters, RO, mixed-bed polishers -> demin; ~190 m3/h raw), firewater, potable, dust suppression, gland/seal water and residue-washing top-up. Most process wash water comes from process condensate (A07/A18, ~650 t/h) and recycled residue-area (RSA) decant/stormwater. Cooling-tower blowdown and RO reject go to residue washing. Fresh water is ~2.7 m3/t.

4) Cooling water.
A 7-cell (6+1) induced-draft counterflow cooling tower (~16,000 m3/h design, ~14,000 normal, range ~10 K) rejects ~165-185 MW. Users:
- Evaporator surface condensers ~50-60 MW
- Precipitation interstage coolers ~45-70 MW (design 60)
- A11 trim coolers ~15 MW
- Oxalate coolers ~15-20 MW
- A15 product fluid-bed coolers ~10-12 MW, if on CW
- Compressor, turbine lube and generator coolers ~10 MW
The water is treated against scale, corrosion and biofouling, with pH and conductivity monitored to catch caustic ingress from process exchangers.

5) Compressed air.
Four oil-free centrifugal compressors (3 duty, 1 standby, ~4,000 Nm3/h each at 8 barg) supply plant air (filter cake blowing, air lances, tools, pneumatic-conveying top-ups) and, through desiccant dryers, instrument air at -40 degC pressure dew point (ISO 8573-1 class 2 for water). Instrument air has priority, through a receiver with a non-return valve.

6) Lime.
Quicklime (CaO ~88-92% available) arrives by road bulk tanker (from the port or a regional kiln) and is blown pneumatically into 2 silos (~1,500 t each, ~14 days at ~8.6 t/h). It is slaked in 2 x 100% detention slakers with hot process condensate: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2, about -1.14 MJ/kg CaO (exothermic), slurry ~75-85 degC. The water:lime ratio is controlled to hold that temperature. Grit is removed, and the 15-20% slurry is stored and circulated round a ring main to causticisation (A19), TCA/filter-aid preparation (A10), digestion/pre-desilication (A05/A06, optional) and residue neutralisation.

7) Fuel.
Natural gas arrives by pipeline at a receiving station for filtration, heating, metering and pressure reduction: ~25-30 barg for the gas turbines and ~4-8 barg for the calciners, boilers, duct burners and kiln. Diesel is stored for the emergency generators, diesel firewater pumps and the mobile fleet.

8) Electrical.
A 132 kV grid connection and main substation, with 11 kV generation and distribution, 6.6/3.3 kV for large motors (mills, compressors, CW pumps, BFW pumps) and 415 V MCCs. Two emergency diesel generators support essential loads (control systems, lube oil, thickener rakes, selected agitators, lighting).

Note for high-temperature (boehmitic) plants: digestion needs steam at ~30-60 bar or molten-salt/hot-oil heating, so the steam cycle has a high-pressure process header and less back-pressure power per tonne of steam.
