equipment.name: Gas turbine generators (cogeneration)
equipment.function: Generate electricity and supply hot exhaust gas to the HRSGs.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (aux boilers and the grid cover the loss of one)
equipment.type_selected: Industrial or aeroderivative gas turbine, ~25-35 MW ISO, dry low-NOx combustor, 11 kV air-cooled generator
equipment.why_this_type: High combined heat-and-power efficiency (~75-80% fuel utilisation) on natural gas; widely used for steam/power supply to refineries in Western Australia.
key_dimensions: Package enclosure ~20 m L x 5 m W x 6 m H; elevated inlet filter house ~8 m x 6 m x 6 m; exhaust transition ~3-3.5 m dia to the HRSG (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.unit: MW each (ISO); ~5-10% lower at tropical ambient

equipment.working_principle: An axial compressor draws in filtered air and compresses it ~15-25 times. Fuel burns in the combustor at constant pressure, and the hot gas expands through the turbine stages, driving both the compressor and the generator. The exhaust (~500 degC, ~14-15% O2) still carries most of the fuel energy and is recovered in the HRSG; its oxygen also supports duct firing.
details_to_model: Acoustic enclosure with doors, ventilation fans and fire suppression (CO2 or water-mist) cylinders
Inlet air filter house with weather hoods, multi-stage filters, inlet duct and silencer
Generator with terminal box, neutral earthing cubicle and bus duct to the step-up transformer
Lube oil skid with fin-fan coolers; fuel gas skid (filter, heater, stop/control valves)
Exhaust diffuser to the HRSG with expansion joint; optional bypass stack with diverter damper
hazards_and_safety: Fuel gas leak/explosion: gas detection in the enclosure, ventilation, ESD
Hot surfaces; noise >100 dB(A) inside the enclosure
Rotating machinery; CO2 fire suppression is an asphyxiation hazard, so lock it out before entry
instrumentation_and_control: Turbine control system (speed, load, exhaust temperature spread)
Vibration (proximity probes), flame detection, gas detection
Generator protection relays, synchroniser
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Inlet filter clogging from bauxite/alumina dust
operating_tips_and_key_points: Change inlet filters on time (refinery dust); run offline/online compressor washes
sources: API 616 Gas Turbines for Petroleum, Chemical and Gas Industry Services
Alinta Pinjarra cogeneration plant supplying the Alcoa Pinjarra refinery - verify

equipment.name: Heat recovery steam generators with duct burners
equipment.function: Recover GT exhaust heat, plus supplementary firing, to raise HP steam for the process and turbine.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal-gas-flow, natural-circulation, single-pressure HRSG with duct burner, superheater, evaporator and economiser; supplementary firing limited to <=850-900 degC (unlined-duct burner practice)
equipment.why_this_type: Single pressure matches a process steam plant, and supplementary firing gives flexibility to follow the steam load. Rating CORRECTED to ~95-100 t/h: the earlier '150 t/h fired' needs ~1,250-1,300 degC firing, i.e. a fully fired water-wall HRSG.
key_dimensions: Casing ~7-8 m W x ~18-22 m H x ~20-25 m L; steam drum ~1.5-1.7 m dia x ~10-12 m on top; stack ~40-45 m x ~3.5-4 m dia (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: heat balance: 90 kg/s x 1.15 kJ/kgK x (850-140) K / ~2,800 kJ/kg = ~94 t/h
vendor practice for duct burners (review finding)

equipment.working_principle: Exhaust gas flows horizontally through banks of finned tubes: the superheater (hottest), then the evaporator, whose riser tubes connect to the steam drum where steam separates from water by natural circulation, then the economiser, which preheats the feedwater. Duct burners in the inlet duct use the ~14-15% O2 left in the GT exhaust to raise the gas temperature when more steam is needed.
details_to_model: Large rectangular insulated casing with external stiffeners, access doors and inlet transition duct
Steam drum on top with safety valves, 2 direct water-level gauges + transmitters, main steam stop valve, non-return valve
Downcomers and riser pipes, headers, blowdown lines to the blowdown tank
Duct burner runners with flame scanners and gas train
Stack with CEMS platform, ladders, aviation lights; platforms at drum and header levels
hazards_and_safety: High-pressure steam: drum safety valves to ASME I / IBR / AS 1228; boiler explosion risk from low water
Furnace explosion: purge before firing (NFPA 85)
Hot surfaces; confined space in the casing
instrumentation_and_control: Three-element drum level control, low-low level trip
Steam pressure/temperature with attemperator
CEMS (NOx, CO, O2)
equipment.materials: Superheater alloy steel (T22/T91); evaporator and economiser CS finned tubes
common_problems: Economiser corrosion at low feedwater temperature
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never bypass the low drum-level trips; blow down as the chemistry requires
sources: ASME BPVC Section I (Power Boilers) / Indian Boiler Regulations / AS 1228
NFPA 85 Boiler and Combustion Systems Hazards Code

equipment.name: Auxiliary gas-fired water-tube boilers
equipment.function: Provide the balance of HP steam (~260 t/h normal) and N-1 back-up when a GT/HRSG or a boiler is offline.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 (hot standby at minimum fire); N-1 across 5 steam generators gives ~500 t/h
equipment.type_selected: Shop-assembled D-type package water-tube boiler with low-NOx burners, FD fan and economiser
equipment.why_this_type: Fast start, high availability, compact. 150 t/h is within the shop-assembled D-type range (up to ~200-270 t/h). Three x 150 t/h (option a) was chosen over two field-erected 200 t/h units because 2 x 200 + 2 x 100 loses 200 t/h on a single failure (N-1 = 400 t/h, short of demand).
key_dimensions: ~150 t/h each; package ~20-22 m L x ~6 m W x ~9-10 m H; individual or common stack ~40 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Gas burns in a water-cooled furnace. Radiant heat boils water in the membrane walls, and convection banks between the steam drum and the mud drum complete the evaporation. A superheater raises the steam temperature, and an economiser recovers flue-gas heat into the feedwater.
details_to_model: Long, boxy casing with burner front (windbox, burner, gas train, flame scanners) and FD fan with silencer at the front
Steam drum on top with safety valves and gauge glasses; economiser on top or rear; flue duct to the stack
Platforms at the burner front and drum level; ladders
Three identical units side by side with a common BFW header and steam header
hazards_and_safety: As for the HRSG: furnace explosion, low water, high-pressure steam
Gas-train leaks: gas detection
instrumentation_and_control: Burner management system (purge, flame safeguard, trips)
Combustion control with O2 trim
Drum level
Plant master steam-pressure controller with fast load pick-up on GT/HRSG trip
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Refractory damage at the burner throat
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep one boiler on hot standby (minimum fire) so it can take load quickly if a GT trips

equipment.name: Back-pressure / extraction steam turbine generator
equipment.function: Expand HP steam to the process pressures while generating electricity.
equipment.type_selected: Multi-stage back-pressure turbine with controlled MP extraction, gearbox and 11 kV generator
equipment.why_this_type: All exhaust steam is used by the process (no condenser loss), giving ~80%+ thermal utilisation of the steam-raising fuel.
key_dimensions: Turbine-gearbox-generator train ~15-18 m long on an ~8 m high concrete table-top; turbine hall with ~50-80 t EOT crane (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (~310 kJ/kg to MP, ~445 kJ/kg to LP at ~75% isentropic efficiency). CHANGED from 35-40

equipment.working_principle: Steam expands through nozzle and blade rows, converting pressure energy to velocity and then to shaft torque. Part of the steam is extracted at MP pressure through a controlled extraction valve, and the rest exhausts at LP header pressure. The turbine is governed on header pressure (back-pressure control) while the generator supplies the grid or island.
details_to_model: Turbine casing with HP inlet stop and control valves (actuator rack), extraction and exhaust nozzles to large-bore headers, lagging
Reduction gearbox (if high-speed), generator with exciter, lube oil console, steam seal system
Table-top foundation with stair; turbine-hall crane; PRDS stations beside
hazards_and_safety: Overspeed (test the trip valves), high-pressure steam, hot surfaces, noise
Lube-oil fire: fire detection and deluge
instrumentation_and_control: Governor, overspeed protection, vibration/axial position monitoring (API 670)
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
operating_tips_and_key_points: Test the trip valves on schedule. The process headers must not lose pressure on a turbine trip, so the PRDS must take over automatically.
sources: API 612 Special-purpose steam turbines; API 670 machinery protection

equipment.name: Pressure-reducing and desuperheating stations (PRDS) and steam headers
equipment.function: Back up the turbine (HP->MP, HP->LP, MP->LP) and keep header pressures constant.
equipment.type_selected: Combined pressure-reducing/desuperheating valve with BFW spray water
equipment.why_this_type: Fast-acting header pressure control on a turbine trip.
key_dimensions: Valves DN300-500 inlet, DN600-900 outlet; headers DN600-1,000 on the main rack (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A control valve drops the steam pressure, and feedwater sprayed in downstream removes the superheat. Pressure and temperature loops trim each station.
details_to_model: Angle-body control valve with large actuator, spray-nozzle assembly, silencer/diffuser, long straight run, drain pots and traps, PSVs on the downstream headers
hazards_and_safety: High noise; steam hammer
instrumentation_and_control: PIC, TIC
equipment.materials: Alloy/CS piping per pressure class
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the PRDS warm (small bleed) for instant response

equipment.name: Deaerators and boiler feedwater pumps
equipment.function: Remove dissolved O2/CO2 from feedwater and pump it at boiler pressure to the HRSGs and boilers.
equipment.type_selected: Spray-tray deaerator on a horizontal storage tank; horizontal multistage barrel/ring-section pumps (BB4/BB5) with VSD or hydrodynamic coupling
equipment.why_this_type: Standard; multistage pumps reach ~80 barg.
key_dimensions: Deaerators 2 x ~300 t/h: head ~2.5 m dia x 5 m; storage ~3.5 m dia x 14 m (~100 m3) each, elevated ~15-20 m above pump suction (engineering estimate)
BFW pumps ~330 m3/h x ~850-900 m, ~1.0-1.3 MW each (2 x 50% + 1 spare)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (heating ~150 t/h make-up and ~300 t/h return condensate)

equipment.working_principle: Feedwater is sprayed into a steam-filled head and heated to saturation, which drives out dissolved gases; these vent with a little steam. The tank stores the deaerated water, and its elevation gives the BFW pumps their NPSH. The multistage pumps raise the pressure through impellers in series.
details_to_model: Elevated structure with horizontal tanks and vertical heads, vent condensers, safety valves, level gauges
Pumps at grade with suction strainers, automatic recirculation (minimum-flow) valves, large motors and lube units
hazards_and_safety: Hot pressurised water flashes if a line breaks
Pump minimum-flow protection to prevent overheating
instrumentation_and_control: Deaerator pressure and level, dissolved-O2 analyser, pump auto-start on low header pressure
equipment.materials: CS; pumps with 13Cr internals
common_problems: Vent valve throttled too far (poor O2 removal)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check dissolved O2 and pH every shift

equipment.name: Condensate return tanks, condensate polishing and pumps
equipment.function: Collect returned clean condensate, verify its purity, polish it and pump it to the deaerators.
equipment.type_selected: Atmospheric CS tanks (internally coated); cartridge/precoat filters + mixed-bed polishers; centrifugal pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Bayer condensate can pick up caustic and alumina through leaks, so polishing and dump protection are essential.
key_dimensions: Tanks 2 x ~1,500 m3 (~13 m dia x 12 m); polishers 3 x ~160 m3/h; pumps ~330 m3/h x ~40 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Online conductivity and sodium analysers on each return line divert contaminated condensate to the process. Accepted condensate is filtered and polished by ion exchange before deaeration.
details_to_model: Analyser shelter with sample coolers, three-way dump valves, filter vessels, resin vessels, regeneration chemical skid
Tanks with vents and overflows; pump set
hazards_and_safety: Hot water; regeneration acid and caustic
instrumentation_and_control: Conductivity, Na and silica analysers; tank levels
equipment.materials: Coated CS / SS
operating_tips_and_key_points: Treat every analyser alarm as real until proven otherwise

equipment.name: Main substation, transformers and emergency diesel generators
equipment.function: Connect to the grid, distribute power at 11 kV and below, and supply emergency power to essential loads.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 substation; 2 grid transformers; generator step-up/unit transformers; 2 EDGs
equipment.type_selected: 132 kV GIS or AIS switchyard; 2 x ~80 MVA 132/11 kV ONAN/ONAF transformers; 11 kV metal-clad switchgear; 2 x ~3 MVA diesel generators
equipment.why_this_type: Firm supply with export capability. The ability to island protects the precipitation and thickener inventories.
key_dimensions: Switchyard ~80 m x 60 m; transformers ~8 m x 5 m x 6 m each with firewalls and oil bunds; EDG containers ~12 m x 3 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Power from the generators and the grid is collected on 11 kV switchboards and distributed by feeders to area substations. Protection relays isolate faults selectively. On total power loss, load shedding and EDG auto-start restore essential loads within seconds, and the refinery restarts in sequence, with agitators started before settled solids harden.
details_to_model: Fenced switchyard with gantries, circuit breakers, disconnectors, CTs/VTs, surge arresters and overhead-line entry
Large oil transformers with radiators, conservator, Buchholz relay, firewalls and oil containment
Switchroom building with cable trenches and battery room; EDG containers with exhaust stacks and day tanks
hazards_and_safety: Electrocution and arc flash: permits, switching procedures, arc-rated PPE
Transformer fire: deluge, firewalls
Diesel fuel
instrumentation_and_control: SCADA/power management system with load shedding
Protection relays (IEC 61850)
common_problems: Dust and caustic mist on outdoor insulators (flashover): insulator washing
operating_tips_and_key_points: Practise the black-start sequence; give priority to precipitator and thickener agitation/rakes

equipment.name: Natural gas receiving station and diesel storage
equipment.function: Receive, filter, heat, meter and reduce pipeline gas for all burners and GTs; store diesel for emergency and mobile use.
equipment.type_selected: Skid-mounted gas station: inlet ESD valve, filter-separators, water-bath or electric heaters, pressure-reduction runs (active/monitor regulators + slam-shut), ultrasonic fiscal meters; API 650 diesel tanks
equipment.why_this_type: Standard pipeline custody transfer and pressure reduction.
key_dimensions: Gas compound ~60 m x 30 m; vent stack ~10-15 m; diesel tanks 2 x ~500 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The gas is cleaned of liquids and dust and heated so that Joule-Thomson cooling across the regulators does not form hydrates or ice. It is then reduced in pressure in two stages and metered for custody transfer. Slam-shut valves protect downstream piping from overpressure.
details_to_model: Fenced compound; yellow piping with flow arrows; filter-separator vessels, heater, regulator runs, meter runs with flow conditioners, vent stack, actuated ESD valve, gas detectors

Diesel fire

equipment.function: Supply fresh water to the refinery and store ~7 days of demand.

Pond with HDPE liner, crest road, inlet/outlet structures, fence, life rings

Water hammer in the long pipeline: surge protection
instrumentation_and_control: Flow, pond level, turbidity

equipment.name: Water treatment and demineralisation plant
equipment.function: Produce clarified/filtered service water and demineralised boiler make-up.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 clarifier, filters, 2 RO trains, 1 mixed bed
equipment.type_selected: Lamella or solids-contact clarifier; multimedia pressure filters; RO (1-pass) + mixed-bed ion-exchange polishers
equipment.why_this_type: Low chemical use and reliable high-purity water for 63-65 bar boilers.

equipment.name: Lime slakers with grit removal and vapour scrubber
equipment.function: Hydrate quicklime with hot water to a reactive Ca(OH)2 slurry and remove grit.
equipment.type_selected: Detention (slurry) slaker with agitated slaking chamber and grit screw (alternatives: paste slaker, or vertical ball-mill slaking for higher reactivity)
equipment.why_this_type: Robust and gives a consistent 15-20% slurry. Controlling the slaking temperature (~75-85 degC) gives fine, reactive hydrate particles, which matters for causticisation efficiency.
key_dimensions: ~10-12 t/h quicklime each; slaking chamber ~25-35 m3 (~3.5 m dia x 3 m) with ~30-45 kW agitator; grit classifier screw ~6 m long; overall ~10 m x 4 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 releases ~1.14 MJ/kg CaO. The water:lime ratio is controlled to hold the slaking temperature. Too much water keeps the temperature too low and DROWNS the lime, giving coarse, low-surface-area hydrate. Too little water lets the slaker overheat and BURN the lime, which also lowers reactivity and risks steam/slurry eruptions. So a falling slaking temperature calls for LESS water per tonne of lime, and a rising temperature towards boiling calls for MORE water. The agitator breaks up agglomerates. The overflow slurry passes a screen, and grit (unburnt stone, silica) is screwed out to a bin.
details_to_model: Box-shaped slaking tank with top agitator, lime inlet chute from the feeder, water inlet with flowmeter and control valve, thermowell
Inclined grit screw with motor; grit discharge chute to a skip
Vapour hood and duct to a wet scrubber with fan and stack
Discharge to the slurry tank via a screen box
hazards_and_safety: Exothermic reaction: steam and hot-slurry eruptions if the slaker is starved of water (burning) or water is added suddenly to a hot dry charge; burns
Lime dust and slurry (pH ~12.5): eye injuries, so eyewash is essential
instrumentation_and_control: Slaking temperature control (water:lime ratio, trimmed by water flow), lime feed rate, agitator current
equipment.materials: CS with wear liners
common_problems: Scaling in the water inlet; grit screw wear
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hold the slaking temperature steady with the water:lime ratio. Low temperature means drowning (cut the water); near-boiling means burning (add water). Lime reactivity drives causticisation efficiency and filter-aid quality.
sources: Lime supplier slaking guides (Carmeuse/Lhoist technical bulletins; National Lime Association) - drowning vs burning terminology - verify
Whittington (1996) Hydrometallurgy 43:13-35 (lime reactivity in the Bayer process)

areas.layout_notes: The power house is a block ~170 m x 110 m beside the steam load centre. It holds the GTs, HRSGs, 3 auxiliary boilers, the STG hall, the deaerator bay, BFW pumps and condensate polishing. It is ~150-300 m from digestion (A06) and evaporation (A18), so the large-bore MP/LP headers stay short on the main pipe rack. The HRSG and boiler stacks (~40-45 m) are on the downwind side of the block. The main 132 kV substation sits next to the power house on the side away from the cooling tower, at least 100-150 m from it to avoid drift and mist on insulators. The cooling tower (7 cells in a row, ~110 m x 18 m, plus the pump pit) lies between precipitation (A12) and evaporation (A18) to keep the CW headers short. Its long axis is perpendicular to the prevailing wind, and it is >=30-50 m from buildings and air intakes. The compressor house is near the power house or the centre of air demand (hydrate filtration A14, calcination/pneumatic conveying A15/A16). The lime area (silos ~30 m tall, slakers, slurry tank) is a ~50 m x 40 m compound beside the refinery access road, near causticisation (A19) and clarification (A08/A10), with a tanker turning circle. The raw water pond (~160 m x 130 m) and water treatment plant are at a site high point or edge, with the firewater tanks and fire pump house nearby. The gas receiving station is at the site boundary near the pipeline entry, >=50-100 m from ignition sources, with gas lines to the power house and calciners on the rack. Diesel storage is next to the EDGs and the mobile-equipment refuelling bay. A main E-W pipe rack spine (~1.2-1.5 km) with N-S branches (2-4 tiers, +6 to +15 m) carries steam, condensate, CW, air, lime and gas to all areas.

decisions.finding: A20 20-HR-001/002 (major, mechanical): HRSG rating of 150 t/h fired is not achievable with duct firing; N-1 steam capacity (~340 t/h) is below demand.
decisions.reason: Own heat balance confirms it: 90 kg/s x ~1.15 kJ/kgK x (850-140) K = ~73 MW, divided by ~2,800 kJ/kg = ~94 t/h; unfired ~35-45 t/h. HRSGs re-rated to 95-100 t/h with firing <=850-900 degC, and the 150 t/h figure removed. Option (a) adopted: a third 150 t/h package boiler (20-BL-003), giving ~650 t/h installed and ~500 t/h N-1. Option (b), 2 x 200 t/h field-erected, was rejected because loss of one 200 t/h unit leaves 400 t/h, below the corrected 450-470 t/h demand. decisions.finding: A18 18-SK-001 (major, HSE): descaling hazards held a placeholder ('H2S? (not expected)') and said hydrogen forms only on contact with Al/Zn; this contradicted A06.
decisions.reason: Fe + H2SO4 -> FeSO4 + H2 on carbon-steel tubes is basic acid-corrosion chemistry, and it gets worse when the inhibitor is depleted. The reviewer's text is applied, LEL monitoring and venting are added to details, instrumentation and the effect hazards, and dissolved-iron tracking is added as an inhibitor-depletion indicator. Now consistent with A06.

decisions.finding: A20 20-SL-401/402 (major, HSE): the slaker principle reversed 'drowning' (it said too hot drowns the lime).
decisions.reason: Lime-industry usage: drowning = too much water / low temperature, giving coarse low-surface-area hydrate; burning = too little water / overheating. The working principle, hazards, control and operating tips are rewritten, including the correct direction for water:lime ratio corrections.
